column1: # ci-unit-weights.tsv — the MEASURED cost of each verification unit, in seconds.
# WHAT THIS IS FOR. `ci-units.sh` packs units into shards longest-first, so it
# needs a cost per unit. Nothing here changes WHAT is verified; it changes only
# how the work is distributed, and a wrong number costs wall-clock balance and
# nothing else. That is why this is dated data with provenance rather than a
# EVERY ROW IS FROM ONE RUN: the receipts of run 34434314424, a full sharded pass on
# `ubuntu-latest` at `cfa8e513`, 2026-09-10. Every unit in the inventory, timed
# on the hardware CI actually pays on, in a single execution — so these numbers
# are comparable with each other, which numbers stitched from several sources
#   (2026-09-11: the 43 rows naming suites removed with the CEO's workspace spec,
#   docs/plans/worktree-spec-2026-09-11.md, were deleted. The totals below are that
#   run's, not the current inventory's; a unit with no row gets DEFAULT_WEIGHT.)
#   150 units, 4915 s serial. The largest, and they are what set the
# THE HISTORY OF THIS FILE IS THE ARGUMENT FOR RE-MEASURING IT. It has been
# rebuilt three times in one day and every version was honestly wrong:
#   a macOS `--only` sweep       put WTI at 1500.1 s, taken at load average 34
#   the quiet-Mac record         had the same harness at 599 s (2026-09-04)
#   run 34423889101's receipts   said 870.7 s, on the runner
#   THIS run, after mutant       says 381.6 s, because `mutation-pool.sh` landed
#   concurrency landed           and made the harnesses concurrent
# Four numbers for one harness, none of them wrong when taken, and only the last
# is the cost CI pays today. A weight is a measurement with a date, never a fact.
# A UNIT WITH NO ROW HERE IS NOT FREE. `ci-units.sh` gives it DEFAULT_WEIGHT and
# packs it as if it were average — never zero, or a batch of new suites all lands
# in one shard and that shard becomes the wall clock.
# HOW TO RE-MEASURE: the coverage job collects every shard's receipts, and
# `ci-shard.sh --verify-receipts` prints the serial cost and the longest shard.
# Read the per-unit durations out of those artifacts and replace these rows with
# the new run id. The plan changes; nothing else does. `ci-units.sh plan` then
# prints the longest shard, which is the number `timeout-minutes` should be
# re-promised against rather than left at whatever survived.
